clue.text: Sail in river flood

indicators.note: in tells us the sail sits within the river's name

parts.note: the Dee is a British river
a lug is a lugsail, a four-cornered sail

explanation.surface: A boat sailing on a river is caught by flooding.
explanation.definitionFit: A deluge is a great flood or downpour of water, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Plastic bag to cope with Costa Concordia?

definitions.meaning: a sack lining a rubbish bin
read as two words, bin a liner: to scrap the wrecked cruise ship

explanation.surface: A joke that a plastic bag is all that is needed for the wrecked cruise ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The Costa Concordia was the cruise liner that capsized off Italy in 2012; to 'bin' it is to throw the liner away.
explanation.definitionFit: A bag of plastic film used to line a rubbish container is the everyday sense.

clue.text: Induct Roger to such knowledge

parts.note: in British slang to roger is to have sex, and sexual knowledge is the legal phrase in question

explanation.surface: Someone is being introduced to a body of learning named after a man called Roger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roger' looks like a name; in British slang it is a verb for having sex, and 'carnal knowledge' is the old legal term for intercourse.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase completes the legal idiom for sexual intercourse, where the adjective means fleshly.

clue.text: Vouch about Southey's first rhyme

indicators.note: about means the confirming verb goes around the next letter

parts.note: to vouch for something is to verify it

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of the poet's name

explanation.surface: Someone attests to the opening lines of a poem by the poet Robert Southey.
explanation.definitionFit: To rhyme, as a verb, is to write in verse, the same as turning something into poetry.

clue.text: Improve Bible class

parts.note: RE is religious education, school Bible study
a form is a school class in Britain

explanation.surface: A teacher wants to raise standards in a scripture lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: To reform something is to make it better by changing it.

clue.text: Little beast causes some trouble in trading area

indicators.note: in places the stirred letters inside the market

parts.note: a mart is a market

indicators.note: trouble suggests the letters of 'some' are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: A small animal makes mischief in a marketplace.
explanation.definitionFit: A marmoset is a small South American monkey, so a little animal.

clue.text: Many interceded without having provided drugs

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the verb wraps around the numeral

parts.note: to intercede between parties is to mediate
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, i.e. many

explanation.surface: Lots of people stepped in to help without supplying any medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: Medicated means treated with or given medicine, which is supplying drugs.

clue.text: Big name in Swansea?

parts.note: mega means huge

explanation.surface: Someone is a celebrity in the Welsh city of Swansea.
explanation.walkthrough: Swansea is in Wales, and this is a Welsh girl's name, so the whole clue also defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's forename of Welsh origin, so one you might hear in a Welsh city.

clue.text: Tough solidity for road transport crossing a bit of rail track

indicators.note: crossing means the vehicle straddles the other pieces, holding them within

parts.note: a bus is road transport

indicators.note: a bit of takes just the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: railway lines make a track

explanation.surface: A bus crossing a railway line shows sturdy build.
explanation.definitionFit: Burliness is strong, heavy build, a tough solidity of frame.

clue.text: Inflexible view of a master of hounds?

parts.note: a hound is a dog
MA is Master of Arts

explanation.surface: An outdated outlook is held by the man in charge of the hunt's hounds.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as DOG MA, a Master of Arts of hounds: hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogma is a set of fixed beliefs held without question, an inflexible view.

clue.text: Untoward?

parts.note: split as un-toward, not towards, i.e. the opposite preposition, moving away

explanation.surface: A single word asking whether something is improper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Untoward' normally means unfortunate; read literally, 'not toward' is the preposition of moving away.
explanation.definitionFit: The opposite of the preposition toward is the one meaning away, origin or departure.

clue.text: Sense about names, as Nigella is this flower

indicators.note: about means the verb wraps around the two letters

parts.note: to sense is to feel
N is name, so NN is names

explanation.surface: A remark about the TV cook Nigella, as if she were a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: Nigella looks like the TV cook Nigella Lawson, but here it is the plant Nigella sativa, called fennel flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Nigella sativa is popularly known as fennel flower, so Nigella is the flower of that name.

clue.text: Some retreat into the stronghold — and they are the leaders

indicators.note: into places the reversed word inside the fortress

parts.note: a fort is a stronghold

indicators.note: retreat means the word goes backwards

explanation.surface: Some troops pull back into the castle, led by their chiefs.
explanation.definitionFit: Those at the very front, leading the rest, are the first in rank.

clue.text: Dark and diffident about a skin blemish

indicators.note: about means the shy word surrounds the blemish

parts.note: diffident means shy
a wart is a growth on the skin

explanation.surface: Someone is gloomy and shy about a mark on their skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Swarthy means dark in complexion.

clue.text: Tale of mystery to undo with difficulty

indicators.note: with difficulty suggests the letters are wrestled into a new order

explanation.surface: A mystery story is hard to unravel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is part of the fodder, so 'difficulty' alone signals the rearrangement of UNDOWITH.
explanation.definitionFit: A whodunit is a detective story built around solving a mystery.

clue.text: Sued over disaster following 80% equine in deli product

indicators.note: following means the rearranged letters come after
80% keeps four of the five letters of the animal, the opening run

parts.note: a horse is an equine

indicators.note: disaster suggests the letters of the two words are wrecked and reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone sues after a horsemeat scandal at a delicatessen.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls the 2013 horsemeat scandal; 'disaster' turns SUEDOVER into DOEUVRES.
explanation.definitionFit: Small savoury appetisers are typical delicatessen goods.

clue.text: Musical score in Abu Dhabi?

parts.note: EMI is a record company
to score is to rate

explanation.surface: A musical score composed in Abu Dhabi.
explanation.definitionFit: Abu Dhabi is one of the seven United Arab Emirates, an example of the term.

clue.text: Prayer for a deceased heretic by the river

parts.note: RIP, rest in peace, is said for the dead
an Arian followed Arius, condemned as a heretic

explanation.surface: A prayer is said for a dead heretic beside a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Riparian means on or relating to a riverbank.

clue.text: Withdraw connection from one liable to miss the bus

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
someone running so late may miss the bus

explanation.surface: Someone who is often late gets cut off from others.
explanation.definitionFit: To isolate is to cut off contact or links with something.

clue.text: See 16
America finds European corn fit for purpose

parts.note: USA is America
blé is the French word for wheat or corn

explanation.surface: The USA judges European grain good enough to use.
explanation.definitionFit: Usable means able to be used for its intended job.

clue.text: Player of loud music told to get packing

indicators.note: told signals a word as heard rather than written

parts.note: a wrapper is packing material

explanation.surface: A noisy musician is sent away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get packing' suggests leaving; here 'packing' is a wrapper.
explanation.definitionFit: A rap artist performs loud, rhythmic spoken music.

clue.text: Oil worker offshore with voice of severity

indicators.note: with voice of means the word for severity as it is pronounced

parts.note: rigour means strictness or severity

explanation.surface: An oil-platform worker speaks harshly.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigger works on an offshore oil rig.

clue.text: Morals in Violet Elizabeth's county

indicators.note: Violet Elizabeth Bott in the Just William books lisps, turning S into TH in speech

parts.note: Essex is an English county

explanation.surface: Moral principles in the home county of a girl called Violet Elizabeth.
explanation.walkthrough: Violet Elizabeth Bott, in Richmal Crompton's Just William stories, lisps; ESSEX in her mouth comes out close to this word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethics are moral principles governing conduct.

clue.text: Bush turns writer

indicators.note: turns means the author's name is read backwards

parts.note: Albert Camus was a French writer

explanation.surface: A President Bush turns author.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumac is a shrub or small tree, so a bush.

clue.text: Oily rag wrung out over chapter's ruling clique

indicators.note: over means the reworked letters cover the abbreviation, holding it inside
wrung out suggests the letters are twisted into a new order

parts.note: CH is the abbreviation for chapter

explanation.surface: An oily rag is wrung out over a chapter of a book.
explanation.definitionFit: An oligarchy is rule by a small group, a ruling clique.

clue.text: 6 all round = 11

parts.note: VI is the Roman numeral six

indicators.note: round means the word is turned back to front

explanation.surface: A sum: six with all around it equals eleven.
explanation.walkthrough: 11 is a football team of eleven players, here Aston Villa.
explanation.definitionFit: Aston Villa is a football club, and a football team is an eleven.

clue.text: Statement on cultivation of nature etc

indicators.note: cultivation of suggests the letters are worked over into a new form

explanation.surface: A remark about the cultivation of nature and so on.
explanation.definitionFit: An utterance is something said, a spoken statement.
